title: How Much of Your Life Are You Still Willing to Sell?
description:
A stable career can give us security, identity, and a life we have spent decades building. But at some point, another question may begin to surface: how much of our remaining time are we still willing to trade for that security?

This essay is not about quitting your job. It is about looking more carefully at the relationship between work and the life around it — the difference between what we are suited for, what we are good at, and what we still want to spend our time doing.

The longer we stay on a path, the harder it can be to imagine leaving it. Education, expertise, professional identity, accumulated experience, and financial stability all become part of the equation. So does the simple fact that the years ahead no longer feel unlimited.

Perhaps the question is not whether we should stay or leave.

Perhaps it is simply this:

How much of your remaining time are you still willing to sell?

A Second Look at Life is a series of quiet, reflective essays about work, time, aging, family, identity, and the choices that shape the second half of life.
